name: DuckDB
model: Tables of typed columns, rich SQL; also queries Parquet, CSV, JSON and Iceberg/Delta files in place; one database file
engine_note: Library linked into your process; columnar row groups, vectorised execution, MVCC; single-file storage plus a write-ahead log
consistency: ACID multi-row transactions; snapshot isolation (docs: repeatable read in Postgres terms), the only level. One process may write at a time (many threads inside it); conflicting writes to the same rows fail and must be retried. Persistent mode writes changes to disk.
scaling: Bigger machine only (one process, larger-than-memory spilling); multi-writer via DuckLake (Postgres catalog) or the beta Quack protocol; MotherDuck runs it as a service.

licence_events.event: DuckLabs (formerly DuckDB Labs) agrees to join AWS; DuckDB stays MIT-licensed, IP held by the non-profit DuckDB Foundation; not a licence change

version_note: v2.0 is in public preview (duckdb.org 2026-09-02 'Try DuckDB v2.0-dev'), not stable.
reach: Reach for it when you want fast SQL over local files or a laptop-sized dataset inside a Python script, notebook or service, with nothing to run.
avoid: Avoid when many processes or users must write the same database at once, or as the live store behind a web app.
escape: analytics over Parquet or a 50 GB export runs in-process, columnar and far faster, with no server to run
chat: Offline analysis of exported messages and usage events, e.g. a notebook computing retention.
notes: Old-notes claim checked against primary sources. VERIFIED: Amazon announcement 'AWS to acquire DuckLabs, the Amsterdam-based company behind DuckDB' (aboutamazon.com, published 2026-08-26, https://www.aboutamazon.com/news/company-news/aws-ducklabs) says 'We are not acquiring the DuckDB open source project, which will remain free and open source under the independent DuckDB Foundation ... and available under the MIT license' and that Hannes Muhleisen and Mark Raasveldt 'will continue leading the team and the open source project's technical direction'. CORRECTIONS: (1) date: announced 2026-08-26 as a signed definitive agreement; the DuckLabs post (https://ducklabs.com/news/2026/08/26/ducklabs-to-join-aws) says effective September 1 and its update says 'The process concluded successfully on Aug 31, 2026'. So 'August 2026' is right for announcement and close. (2) name: the company is currently called DuckLabs, not DuckDB Labs. It was founded as DuckDB Labs in 2021 and renamed to DuckLabs on 2026-05-27 ('DuckDB Labs Becomes DuckLabs', https://ducklabs.com/news/2026/05/27/duckdb-labs-becomes-ducklabs.html); duckdblabs.com now redirects to ducklabs.com. So 'DuckLabs' in the old note is correct; write 'DuckLabs (formerly DuckDB Labs)'. (3) DuckLabs becomes an AWS subsidiary (duckdb.org post 2026-08-26, https://duckdb.org/2026/08/26/ducklabs-to-join-aws.html); the team stays in Amsterdam; the Foundation adds a stakeholder/technical advisory board. Licence file history shows no licence change (MIT). No Jepsen analysis.
